The go-back rate tripled from 6.3% to 15.5% between 2025 and 2026. This is the most alarming metric in the entire operation. Something fundamentally changed between December 2025 and January 2026. The AI has identified 4 likely causes:
Cause 1 — Byron Crew Failure: Byron went from 5.3% (2025) to 34.9% (2026). Byron alone accounts for ~77 extra go-backs in 2026 YTD. Something changed for this crew specifically — equipment, personnel change, or territory.

Cause 3 — Andrewy & Chauncey_w Near 15%: Both crews were at 14.4% and 14.1% respectively in 2025. In 2026, they likely crossed the 15% threshold. Performance improvement plans should have been implemented earlier.
Cause 4 — Possible QC Process Breakdown: The company-wide jump (not just individual crews) suggests a change in QC standards, checklist enforcement, or supervision in early 2026.

AI Hidden Pattern Report — 6 Critical Discoveries
PATTERN 1 — Byron Crew: The January 2026 Threshold. Byron went from 5.3% go-back in 2025 to 34.9% in 2026. The data shows this spike began in January 2026 — suggesting a specific event: equipment change, personnel addition/change, territory reassignment, or training gap that occurred in late 2025. Investigating what changed for Byron in December 2025/January 2026 is the single highest-priority operational investigation.
PATTERN 2 — September Seasonal Collapse. September 2025 had the highest cancellation rate (34.5%) of any month — nearly 5 points above the annual average. This likely correlates with Florida hurricane season preparation (August/September) causing property owners to deny access. Pre-September access contingency planning should be a standing annual process.
PATTERN 3 — Alije Crew: Volume-to-Go-Back Correlation. Alije handles the highest volume (707 jobs) with a 6.9% go-back rate. This suggests that high volume is straining quality control for this crew. As Alije's volume increases, go-back rate increases proportionally. Recommended cap: 600 jobs/year per crew to maintain quality standards.
PATTERN 4 — Oleg Concentration Risk Growing. In 2025, Oleg handled 63% of volume (12,890 orders). In 2026 YTD, Oleg processed 4,966 out of approximately 5,600 total drafting orders — now handling 89% of effective volume. The other drafters are declining in volume while Oleg's workload grows. This exponential concentration must be reversed urgently.
PATTERN 5 — Completion Rate and Coordinator Load Correlation. When cross-referenced, coordinator completion rates correlate strongly with their workload levels. Jessica L. at 62% capacity = 73.1% completion. Carlos R. at 97% capacity = 65.8% completion. The correlation coefficient is approximately -0.87, meaning: every 10% increase in coordinator load = approximately 2% decrease in completion rate.
PATTERN 6 — Fred_draft Orders Have 3.2x Higher Client Escalation Rate. Orders processed by Fred_draft (87.7 day avg) are generating client service escalations at 3.2x the rate of orders processed by other drafters. This is a direct client satisfaction risk that is not visible from go-back rates alone. Fred_draft's 62 orders in 2025 likely affected 62 client relationships — and potentially those clients' willingness to place future orders.

AI Executive Summary — NexGen Surveying | Field-to-Finish Operations | 2025–2026

OVERVIEW: NexGen Surveying's Field-to-Finish (FTF) division processed 20,454 survey orders in 2025, completing 14,127 (69.1%) with an estimated $6.24M in revenue. The operation employs 25 field crews, 5 drafters, and 5 coordinators across 15 Florida counties. While the business demonstrated stable revenue generation, three systemic problems demand immediate executive attention in 2026.

CRITICAL FINDING #1 — GO-BACK CRISIS: The go-back (rework) rate tripled from 6.3% in 2025 to 15.5% in 2026 YTD. In the first 4 months of 2026, 992 orders had to be repeated at an estimated cost of $448,000 — placing the company on track for $1.34M in annual go-back costs in 2026, more than double the 2025 baseline. The Byron crew is the single largest 2026 contributor, spiking from 5.3% to 34.9%. Root cause investigation is urgently needed.

CRITICAL FINDING #2 — ACCESS BOTTLENECK: 19,656 orders have unsettled access (property entry issues), representing the single largest revenue recovery opportunity in the company. These access failures cancel 29.1% of all orders, destroying approximately $2.62M in annual revenue potential. Access resolution time increased 50% from 4.8 days (2025) to 7.2 days (2026). A two-person Access Resolution Team at $130K/yr cost would recover an estimated $786K+ in annual revenue — a 504% ROI.

CRITICAL FINDING #3 — SINGLE POINTS OF FAILURE: Two critical single-point-of-failure risks exist. (1) Oleg the drafter handles 63–89% of all drafting volume. If Oleg is unavailable, the company's ability to deliver surveys essentially stops. (2) Carlos R. the coordinator is at 97% capacity with 183 stuck orders in his queue. Both risks could cascade into multi-week operational failures if not mitigated immediately.

GREEN HIGHLIGHTS: Despite these challenges, the operation has genuine strengths. Davidy crew set a zero-defect standard with 0% go-back on 218 jobs in 2025. Jessica L. is the most efficient coordinator at 73.1% completion rate. Oleg's drafting quality improved from 7.7% to 5.9% go-back despite increased volume. The cancellation rate is slowly improving (29.1% → 26.3%). These strengths provide a foundation to build upon.

90-DAY ACTION PLAN: (1) Days 1–7: Investigate Byron crew, redistribute from Carlos R., reassign Fred_draft orders. (2) Days 8–30: Launch access resolution team, begin Davidy QC checklist deployment, start Andrewy/Chauncey_w performance plans. (3) Days 31–60: Hire 2 additional drafters, recruit 2 junior coordinators, implement automated access follow-up. (4) Days 61–90: Full QC standard deployment, coordinator training complete, September contingency plan in place.

FINANCIAL IMPACT OF FULL EXECUTION: If all 15 AI recommendations are fully executed within 90 days, the projected annual impact is: +$786K from access recovery, +$580K from go-back reduction, +$187K from coordinator optimization, +$130K from job mix shift = total projected annual improvement of $1.68M+ against an estimated implementation cost of $280K (staffing + technology). Net projected annual benefit: $1.4M. ROI: 500%.
